summary: Official September FOMC minutes resolved the prior run's decisive check. All participants supported the September 25 bp hike and most judged another increase likely appropriate by year-end, but officials split over whether tightening was precautionary insurance against energy/supply shocks or required to restrain demand. With October hike odds below 20%, December odds near 83%, and the long end still stressed, the durable state becomes DIVIDED_CONDITIONAL_TIGHTENING_WITH_LONG_END_STRESS rather than a mechanical every-meeting hiking cycle.

evidence.finding: All participants supported the 25 bp hike to 3.75%-4.00%; most saw another increase likely appropriate by year-end; several viewed policy as not restrictive or only mildly restrictive. Staff raised the 2026-2028 inflation forecast, strengthened the growth outlook, and saw inflation risks skewed upward.

The September hike rationale split between insurance against spreading supply shocks and a more restrictive response to demand inflation; investors expected an October hold followed by a likely December hike.
October hike odds were 19.4%, down from about 38% a week earlier, while December hike odds were 83%; the dollar index was up 0.32% at 102.24.
QQQ -0.24%, TLT -0.15%, UUP +0.48%, GLD -1.68%, and BTC/USD -2.47%. These observations establish contemporaneous state, not minutes-only causality.
